annotations.title: Microsoft Teams Pricing for Business: Plans & Features
Learn about spaces - Google Chat Help

content.text:
For most small companies, the best choice depends more on your existing work suite than on chat features alone.

| Best for | Tool | Why it stands out | Watch-out |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Best overall default** | **Slack** | Excellent channels, threads, search, integrations, quick calls (“huddles”), and easy collaboration with clients/vendors through Slack Connect. | The free plan is limited to 90 days of accessible history; Pro is **$7.25/user/month annually**. ([slack.com](https://slack.com/help/articles/115003205446-Slack-plans-and-features?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Microsoft-based companies** | **Microsoft Teams** | Best value if you already use Microsoft 365: chat, meetings, files, tasks, and Office collaboration are tightly connected. Teams Essentials is **$4/user/month annually**; Microsoft 365 Business Basic is **$6/user/month annually** and adds business email, web/mobile Office apps, and 1 TB storage per user. | Can feel heavier and more complicated than Slack for a very small team. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-teams/compare-microsoft-teams-business-options?msockid=19ff77b865aa6ce63920611b64a46d96&utm_source=openai)) |
| **Google Workspace companies** | **Google Chat** | The sensible low-friction option if your work already lives in Gmail, Drive, Docs, Calendar, and Meet. Spaces support threads, file sharing, tasks, and apps. Google Workspace Business Starter is currently **$7/user/month with an annual commitment**. | Less robust as an integration hub and less polished for fast-moving chat than Slack. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/chat/answer/7659784?hl=en-EN&utm_source=openai)) |
| **Async / technical teams** | **Zulip** | Best for keeping conversations organized: each message belongs to a channel *and topic*, which greatly reduces noisy, sprawling threads. Cloud Standard is **$6.67/user/month annually**; its free plan has 10,000 searchable messages. | The topic-based workflow takes a little onboarding. ([docs.zulip.com](https://docs.zulip.com/zulip-cloud/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Self-hosting / data control** | **Rocket.Chat** | A strong choice when you need to run chat on your own infrastructure. Its community edition is open source, and its self-managed Starter offering is listed as free for up to 50 users. | Someone on your team must own security, upgrades, backups, and administration. ([content.rocket.chat](https://content.rocket.chat/hubfs/Community-and-Premium-Editions-Feature-Overview.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |

### My practical picks

- **Choose Slack** if you have 5–75 people, use lots of SaaS tools, and want the least-risk “everyone will understand this” option.
- **Choose Teams** if you already pay for Microsoft 365 or need chat and video meetings tightly paired with Office files.
- **Choose Google Chat** if you already pay for Google Workspace and want to avoid another app and subscription.
- **Choose Zulip** if your team is remote, technical, international, or tired of chat becoming an unsearchable firehose.
- **Choose Rocket.Chat** only if privacy, on-premises hosting, or customization is a real requirement—not merely a preference.

### A simple decision rule

1. **Already on Microsoft 365?** Start with Teams.  
2. **Already on Google Workspace?** Start with Google Chat.  
3. **Neither—and integrations/client collaboration matter?** Use Slack Pro.  
4. **Need calm, highly organized async communication?** Use Zulip.  
5. **Need control of where data lives?** Evaluate Rocket.Chat.  

For a typical small U.S. company, I’d shortlist **Slack Pro, Teams, and Google Chat** first, then run a two-week trial using real projects—not a demo channel.
